svg.data-title: T.S. of the small intestine (ileum) wall

g.data-info: The hollow space of the ileum through which digested food passes.
A single layer of columnar cells with microvilli covering each villus, absorbing digested food molecules.
The inner lining layer of loose connective tissue that supports the villi and crypts.
Tube-shaped pits between villi whose cells divide to replace the epithelium and secrete intestinal juice.
A cell in the epithelium that secretes mucus to lubricate and protect the intestinal lining.
A blind-ended lymph vessel in the centre of each villus that absorbs fatty acids and glycerol.
A dense network of blood capillaries in each villus that absorbs glucose and amino acids into the blood.
A thin sheet of smooth muscle at the base of the mucosa that moves the villi.
A layer of connective tissue carrying larger blood vessels, lymph vessels and nerves.
An inner ring of smooth muscle that contracts to narrow the gut, helping to push food along by peristalsis.
An outer layer of smooth muscle running along the gut that shortens it during peristalsis.
The thin, smooth outer membrane that covers the gut and reduces friction with other organs.
